validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. The 'Equitrans Allenghy Valley Connector' segment (sheet's spelling of Allegheny) is the Allegheny Valley Connector (AVC), a FERC-regulated natural-gas transmission-and-storage system in southwestern/central Pennsylvania, documented by (1) EQT Midstream Partners LP's 2016-10-13 8-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1540947) announcing EQM's $275M acquisition of AVC from EQT Corporation effective 2016-10-01; (2) EQM Midstream Partners' FY2016 10-K and EQT Corporation's FY2016 10-K, both filed 2017-02-09, corroborating the acquisition and describing a 2017 AVC 'modernization' project; and (3) three FERC Natural Gas Act dockets spanning 2015-2026 (CP15-553-000, CP19-218-000, CP26-73-000), all filed by 'Equitrans, L.P.' under its blanket certificate Docket No. CP96-532-000, confirming AVC is an active, currently-operating system as recently as January 2026. Not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate FERC-regulated natural-gas transmission pipeline with associated underground storage (PipelineType=transmission, Fuel=Gas) -- confirmed by both the SEC filings ('FERC-regulated transmission pipeline') and the FERC dockets themselves (Natural Gas Act section 7 / blanket-certificate filings). DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION: per the orchestrator's cross-row brief, P6895 ('Equitrans Mainline'), P6896 (this row, AVC), and P6897 ('Ohio Valley Connector', separately confirmed in this batch's P4454 shard as FERC docket CP15-41) are three genuinely DISTINCT Equitrans systems, not duplicates of one another or of P4454 (the 2022 Ohio Valley Connector Expansion). Route-geometry check: P6896's digitized route (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P6896.geojson, single MultiLineString feature, 148 points, lon -80.25..-78.89, lat 40.15..41.07, north-central/south-central PA) is geographically distinct from P6895's WV->PA route (315 points, starting at the Corona WV compressor station) and P6897's OH->WV route (33 points) -- it does not overlap either. The three rows share only an erroneous copied Capacity figure (see spec finding below), not a physical pipe. SPEC (see separate finding): Capacity=4,400.00 MMcf/d recorded on the sheet is a system-wide EQM Midstream Partners TOTAL-fleet or Equitrans Mainline-scale throughput figure, not AVC's own capacity -- AVC's actual figures (per the operator's own 2016 8-K/10-Ks) are ~209 miles of transmission pipeline, 450 MMcf/d of transmission capacity, and 11 Bcf (11.2 Bcf per FERC Docket CP15-553) of working-gas storage capacity, all far below 4,400 MMcf/d.

validity.researcher_notes: Per the orchestrator's addendum: P6895, P6896 (this row), and P6897 all carry an identical Capacity=4,400.00 MMcf/d with blank endpoints -- almost certainly one EQM/Equitrans Midstream system- or corporate-level figure (e.g. total interstate transmission portfolio throughput) copied onto three separate, much-smaller Equitrans systems, rather than a genuine per-system capacity. AVC is specifically NOT a greenfield 4,400 MMcf/d trunk: it is the ~209-mile, leased-then-acquired (EQM acquired it from EQT for $275M effective 2016-10-01, having previously operated it under a lease) Allegheny Valley Connector transmission-and-storage system serving Peoples Natural Gas under a firm reservation through 2034. The operator's own 2016-10-13 8-K states plainly: 'The Allegheny Valley Connector (AVC) is regulated by [FERC] and includes approximately 209 miles of transmission pipeline and 11 Bcf of working gas storage capacity. The AVC system has 450 MMcf per day of transmission capacity.' This 450 MMcf/d transmission-capacity figure is corroborated in kind (not in the identical number, but in the same order of magnitude and system) by FERC Docket CP15-553-000 (Federal Register, 2015-10-08), an independent, non-EQT-family publisher, which restates AVC's STORAGE-side deliverability at 246 MMcf/d (down from 260 MMcf/d) and working-gas capacity at 11.2 Bcf (matching the 8-K's rounded '11 Bcf') -- i.e. every AVC-specific figure found across two independent publisher families (SEC/EQT corporate family, and FERC/Federal Register) clusters in the low hundreds of MMcf/d, nowhere near 4,400. TIER: the specific value being proposed here (450.00 MMcf/d transmission capacity, the metric matching the sheet's CapacityUnits) is stated only in the EQT/EQM/Equitrans corporate-filing family (the 2016 8-K and both FY2016 10-Ks are ONE origin per the addendum's SEC-filer rule) -- so this fill is staged at medium/independent=false, not high, even though the broader conclusion that 4,400 is wrong is corroborated by the separate FERC-docket family.

AVC is a legacy system, not a recent proposal. Every FERC docket found (CP15-553 in 2015, CP19-218 in 2019, CP26-73 in 2026) references Equitrans' underlying blanket certificate 'Docket No. CP96-532-000' as the system's original NGA authorization, and the 2016 EQT 10-K traces AVC's corporate retention back to the 2013 'Equitable Gas Transaction' (in which EQT sold its Equitable Gas Company LDC business but retained AVC, then valued at $140.9M) -- both facts place AVC's true origin well before 1996-2013, with no proposal-stage record locatable. Searched: SEC EDGAR full-text search ('Allegheny Valley Connector'), the FERC/Federal Register docket family, and the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv -- no 'Allegheny' project_name match, confirmed via direct grep). No proposal year found; left UNRESOLVED rather than inferring one.

No original-construction year located -- AVC predates the sources available (see Proposal note re: CP96-532-000 blanket certificate and the 2013 Equitable Gas Transaction). What WAS found are later replacement/modernization projects, which are not the segment's original construction: (1) EQT's FY2016 10-K describes a 2017 'AVC modernization' project, 'the replacement of approximately 20 miles of pipeline', part of $60-80M in 2017 transmission-expansion capex; (2) FERC Docket CP19-218 (2019) describes the 'Bare Pipe Replacement Project', abandoning 3.85 miles of 20-inch TP-4555 pipe and replacing it with 3.92 miles of 20-inch pipe in Westmoreland County, PA. Neither is a construction-year proxy for the whole system; left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a proxy year, per standing rule 2.

AVC was already an established, operating system before the 2013 Equitable Gas Transaction and before the CP96-532-000 blanket certificate referenced in every later FERC docket -- both point to a pre-1996 (likely decades older, legacy) in-service date, but neither source states a specific year. Searched SEC EDGAR full-text, the FERC/Federal Register docket family, and the EIA workbook (no AVC row). Left UNRESOLVED rather than recording an inferred year without a citable source.

summary: P6896 = the Allegheny Valley Connector (AVC), a real, independently confirmed ~209-mile FERC-regulated transmission-and-storage system in Cambria/Clarion/Allegheny/Westmoreland Counties, PA, acquired by EQM from EQT for $275M in 2016 (previously leased) and still actively operated by Equitrans, L.P./Equitrans Midstream Corporation as of a January 2026 FERC filing -- not a duplicate of sibling rows P6895 (Equitrans Mainline, WV->PA) or P6897 (Ohio Valley Connector, OH->WV), whose routes are geographically distinct. Main finding: the sheet's Capacity=4,400 MMcf/d is a system/portfolio-level figure copied onto all three Equitrans rows -- AVC's own capacity is 450 MMcf/d transmission (plus 11-11.2 Bcf working-gas storage / 246 MMcf/d storage deliverability per an independent FERC docket), staged as a spec concern with cross_row_leads to P6895 and P6897.
